title: Frontend: Shortest Distance from Source (Dijkstra's Algorithm)
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Shortest Distance from Source (Dijkstra's Algorithm). This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Implement solution({count,edges,source}) for directed nonnegative weights. Return distances, null for unreachable. Use dense Dijkstra minimum-unvisited selection. Any negative edge throws Negative edge.
constraints: Define solution(input) in plain JavaScript. Return the documented JSON-compatible value or throw the documented validation error. Each case receives a fresh input.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Use a min-heap of candidate distances, initialize the source to zero, and relax outgoing edges from the smallest valid entry.
alternativeApproaches: Add path reconstruction and compare with Bellman–Ford when negative weights are permitted.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Zero-weight edge; unreachable node; repeated improvements.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
